29-013.r: UP Legislative Council → Governor nominates 1/10 of members (per book); nominees have special knowledge of literature, science, arts, co-operative movement, social service (Article 171(3)).

29-015.r: State Legislative Council → permanent House, cannot be dissolved; members serve six years, one-third retire every second year; elects own Chairman; one-third elected by Assembly.
29-015.t: Industrialists are not a category that elects Council members.

29-017.r: State Legislative Council → cannot be dissolved but can be abolished (Article 169); member's tenure 6 years. Rajya Sabha: neither; Lok Sabha and Assemblies: dissolved, not abolished.
29-017.h: Council: abolish yes, dissolve no; Rajya Sabha: neither.

29-019.r: Madhya Pradesh has no Legislative Council though Seventh Amendment Act, 1956 provides for it; 6 bicameral States: UP, Maharashtra, Bihar, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana.

29-020.r: Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh → unicameral; Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Bihar, Maharashtra → bicameral (have Legislative Council).

29-024.r: After 1956 reorganisation, 7 of 14 States were bicameral: UP, Bihar, Bombay, Madras, Mysore, Punjab, West Bengal; Councils abolished: West Bengal 1969, Punjab 1970, Tamil Nadu 1986.
29-024.c: No answer printed (*): the correct number, 7, is not among the options.

29-025.r: Article 170 → State Legislative Assembly: minimum 60, maximum 500 members, directly elected; Sikkim is an exception.

29-027.r: State Assembly → not more than 500 members, not 450 (Article 170(1)); minimum age to be chosen to the Assembly → 25 years.

29-029.r: Article 170 → composition and direct election of Legislative Assemblies; Article 176 → Governor's special address; Article 178 → Speaker and Deputy Speaker.

29-030.r: Minimum age → Legislative Assembly member 25 years (Article 173(b)); Legislative Council member 30 years.
29-030.h: Upper House, higher age: Council 30, Assembly 25.

29-031.r: Anglo-Indian representation in State Assemblies → was under Article 333 (Governor could nominate one member); this arrangement was later discontinued.
29-031.c: No answer printed (*): Article 333 was right when asked, but the nomination provision no longer applies.

29-032.r: Uttar Pradesh has the largest Legislative Assembly (403 members), more than Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Maharashtra.

29-033.r: Himachal Pradesh Assembly → 68 seats; Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya → 60 each.

29-034.r: Manipur Assembly → 60 members (not 62); Goa → 40; Uttarakhand → 70; Uttar Pradesh → 403.

29-035.r: J&K split (5 August 2019): Jammu & Kashmir → UT with legislature; Ladakh → UT without legislature; separate Lieutenant Governors.

29-036.r: State Assembly elections → conducted by Election Commission of India (Article 324).
29-036.t: Not the State Election Commission, even though these are State elections.
hi: Election Commission of India (भारत निर्वाचन आयोग)

29-037.r: Disqualification of a State legislator (grounds in Article 191(1)) → Governor's decision is final (Article 192), acting on Election Commission's opinion.

29-038.r: Final decision on disqualification of an MLA → Governor (Article 192), who must obtain and follow the Election Commission's opinion.

29-039.r: Disqualification of MLAs for reasons other than the Tenth Schedule → decided by Governor, according to Election Commission's opinion (Article 192).
29-039.t: Tenth Schedule cases are not decided by the Governor.

29-040.r: Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker (Article 179(b)).
29-040.t: Not the Governor or CM: the Speaker's resignation goes to the Deputy Speaker.

29-041.r: Speaker vacates office if he ceases to be Assembly member, resigns (to Deputy Speaker) or is removed by resolution; not immediately on dissolution (Article 179).

29-042.r: After Assembly dissolution, Speaker stays in office until immediately before the first sitting of the new Assembly (Article 179).

29-043.r: Newly elected Speakers: Ramesh Tawadkar → Goa; Kultar Sandhwan → Punjab; T. Satyabrat → Manipur; Ritu Khandari → Uttarakhand.

29-044.r: Ramkishore Shukla → has held Protem Speaker, Speaker and Deputy Speaker posts in Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly.

29-045.r: Vidhan Sabha of a State is prorogued by the Governor (Article 174(2)).

29-046.r: Governor addresses the Assembly at the first session after each general election and first session of each year; where State has no rule, Lok Sabha rules apply.

29-047.r: Order of MP Assembly proceedings → oath or affirmation → Governor's address → introduction of Ministers → mention of death.

29-048.r: Rajasthan Assembly adjournment motion → needs Speaker's consent; specific matter of recent occurrence; only one per sitting; cannot raise a question of privilege.

29-049.r: Rajasthan Assembly Committee on Subordinate Legislation → examines 'orders' and Bill provisions delegating powers (Rules 240, 241); Speaker does not refer such Bills to it.

29-050.r: Quorum of a House of State Legislature → ten members or one-tenth of total members, whichever is greater (Article 189(3)).
29-050.t: It is 'whichever is greater', not 'whichever is less'.

29-051.r: Rajasthan Assembly rules → Home Department's estimates do not come under Estimates Committee 'A'.

29-052.r: State Legislative Assembly takes part in electing the President, Rajya Sabha members and Legislative Council members; not the Vice-President.
29-052.t: MLAs vote for the President but not for the Vice-President.

29-053.r: State Legislature business → in State official language(s), Hindi or English (Article 210(1)); Advocate General cannot vote; conduct of SC/HC Judges cannot be discussed.

29-054.r: Contingency Fund of the State → placed at the disposal of the Governor for urgent or unforeseen expenditure.

29-055.r: Contingency Fund of the State → established by the State Legislature by law; placed at Governor's disposal for advances on unforeseen expenditure.

29-056.r: Article 162 → Extent of executive power of State: covers matters on which the State Legislature can make laws.

29-057.r: State Legislature Articles: 168 → constitution of Legislature; 178 → Speaker and Deputy Speaker; 195 → salaries of members; 199 → definition of Money Bills.

29-058.r: Ordinary bill passed by Assembly → Legislative Council can hold it 3 months first time (Article 197), about 4 months in all; Vidhan Sabha Speaker decides Money Bill.

29-061.r: State Money Bills → introduced only in Legislative Assembly; Council returns it within 14 days with recommendations (Article 198(2)), which Assembly may accept or reject.

29-062.r: Budget leaked before presentation in Assembly → Finance Minister must take individual responsibility and resign (oath of secrecy; Official Secrecy Act, 1923).

29-063.r: State Money Bill → introduced only on Governor's recommendation (Article 207(1)), never in Legislative Council; matters listed in Article 199(1)(a)-(f).

29-064.r: Chief Minister → appointed by the Governor under Article 164(1).

29-065.r: Governor acts on advice of Council of Ministers headed by CM, except where Constitution requires his discretion (Article 163(1)); so 'all functions on CM's advice' is wrong.

29-066.r: 91st Amendment Act, 2003 → Article 164(1A): State Council of Ministers, including CM, cannot exceed 15% of Assembly members.

29-067.r: State Council of Ministers including CM → minimum 12, maximum fifteen per cent of Assembly members (Article 164(1A)).
29-067.h: Floor 12 ministers, ceiling fifteen per cent.

29-068.r: Chief Minister → formally appointed by Governor (Article 164(1)) but chosen by majority party members in Assembly; not selected by the Governor.

29-069.r: Non-member Minister in a State → may continue six consecutive months; ceases to be Minister if not elected to State Legislature by then (Article 164(4)).

29-071.r: Salaries and allowances of State Ministers → fixed by State Legislature by law (Article 164(5)); until then as in the Second Schedule.

29-072.r: Article 167 → CM's duties: communicate to Governor all Council of Ministers' decisions on State affairs and legislative proposals; furnish information the Governor calls for.

29-074.r: Courts cannot inquire into ministers' advice to the Governor (Article 163(3)); State Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to Legislative Assembly (Article 164(2)).
29-074.c: No answer printed (*): the book confirms the Assertion but does not settle the Reason.

29-075.r: State Council of Ministers → collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly (Article 164(2)); Ministers hold office during Governor's pleasure (Article 164(1)).

29-076.r: J&K Chief Minister's tenure → earlier 6 years (Assembly term), not fixed, lasts while he has majority; J&K Reorganisation Act 2019 fixed Assembly term at 5 years.
29-076.c: No answer printed (*): the term was 6 years when asked but is now 5, so no single option fits.

29-077.r: First woman Chief Minister of an Indian State → Sucheta Kriplani, Uttar Pradesh, 1963.

29-079.r: First CM of Madhya Pradesh → Pt. Ravishankar Shukla (1 November to 31 December 1956); State executive: Articles 153 to 167, Part VI.

29-080.r: Govind Narayan Singh (fifth CM of Madhya Pradesh) → never Leader of the House in MP Legislative Assembly during his tenure.

29-081.r: State Secretariat → apex wing of State administration; main force forming the principles of procedure for State Government's work.

29-083.r: In the State Secretariat, every file goes to the Cabinet through the Chief Secretary.

29-084.r: After Ayodhya incident (1992), Assemblies of UP, MP, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan were dissolved; Bihar's was not (it came under President's rule in 1995).

29-085.r: Andhra Pradesh → proposed reservation for Muslims in jobs and education (2004, struck down by High Court); 2007 → cut to 4 per cent within 50% limit.

29-086.r: Goa → only State with a Common Civil Code, based on Portuguese Civil Code of 1867 (applied 1870); Uttarakhand enforced Uniform Civil Code on 27 January 2025.
